headline: All majors underwater on the 200-day; funding elevated but positioning lopsided long; whales moving coin to cold storage while retail fear sits at 29.
paragraphs: The regime is down across the board. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, BNB, Doge, and Cardano are all trading below their 200-day simple moving averages, and none has a golden cross in place. Bitcoin sits 49.1 percent off its 12-month high of $124,740, Ethereum 61.3 percent down from $4,818, and the damage compounds in the alts: Cardano is 80.7 percent below $0.9631. The 90-day range tells part of the story: Bitcoin has oscillated between $58,566 and $81,059, a band that contains a year's worth of volatility. This is a bear market structure, and the tape does not lie about it.

Momentum is mixed and revealing a split. Bitcoin's RSI sits at 46.2 and MACD is below signal, consistent with downtrend rest but no turn. Ethereum reads 48.4 on RSI with the same MACD posture, also neutral-to-weak. But three assets show MACD above signal despite all being below the 200-day: Solana, BNB, and Doge. This is the only green flag the tape shows, and it is a narrow one. BNB has stretched to RSI 65.8, which is overbought in isolation and unusual given the macro downtrend; it has moved 1.84 percent higher in the last 24 hours and 6.06 percent over seven days. Cardano, meanwhile, has surged 27.4 percent over 30 days while still 80.7 percent below its 12-month peak and MACD above signal. These are small boats catching tide in a falling river, not evidence of regime change.

Derivatives positioning is expensive and crowded long. Bitcoin funding stands at 0.01 percent per eight hours (annualized 11 percent), and Ethereum sits at the same rate; these are high levels, meaning longs are paying to hold the carry. Open interest on Bitcoin is $2.154 billion and on Ethereum $1.373 billion, both substantial pools. The long-to-short ratio on Bitcoin is 1.63, on Ethereum 1.98, on Solana 2.3, on XRP 3.57, and on Doge 4.7. That last number is extreme: nearly five longs for every short. Liquidations over 24 hours show far more long pain than short pain: Bitcoin liquidated $6.22 million in long positions against $459,000 in shorts; Ethereum liquidated $7.98 million long against $1.22 million short. Solana liquidated $1.39 million long against $59,000 short. When funding is high and longs outnumber shorts by three or four to one, the structure is fragile. A move down tests the thesis.

Whale flows show cold storage accumulation while stablecoins shrink. Over the past 24 hours, $185.4 million in net crypto value moved off exchanges, with Bitcoin accounting for $129.3 million and Ethereum $56.2 million. The biggest single moves were Bitcoin out of Kraken ($128.9 million), Bitcoin out of OKEx ($73.5 million), and USDT out of Bitfinex ($169.9 million). This is large holders taking possession and stablecoin holders moving to fiat or sidelines. The seven-day rolling window shows a chop, though: the four-week lookback reads negative $225 million, then positive $1.01 billion, then positive $1.10 billion, then negative $394 million. The pattern is volatile, not a clear trend. Stablecoin float stands at $305.4 billion and has declined 1.38 percent over 30 days, so dry powder is modest.

The Fear and Greed index sits at 29 (Fear territory) with a 30-day range of 22 to 33. The crowd is scared, and the tape partially agrees: spot ETF flows went negative on August 10 (Bitcoin down $144.6 million, Ethereum down $14.6 million), though the five-session net is still positive (Bitcoin $550.6 million, Ethereum $241 million). Traditional finance has sent coins in, but today's pulse is out. That disagreement matters. Whales are moving Bitcoin to custody while retail sentiment sours; this can be accumulation into weakness, or it can be early capitulation before the pain deepens.

Watch for a flip in Bitcoin's long-to-short ratio and funding rate. If the 1.63 long-to-short ratio breaks below 1.3 while funding stays positive, it signals longs have begun to cave; a simultaneous drop in funding into negative territory would confirm panic exit. Alternatively, if Bitcoin can hold above the $58,566 level from its 90-day low and ETH above $1,566, and if BNB and Doge MACD momentum builds with RSI follow-through, a second-stage bounce becomes plausible. Bitcoin network difficulty is declining 1.1 percent into the next retarget (1,608 blocks remain), which is consistent with hashpower capitulation in a bear market. The data does not forecast the next move, but it flags where friction lives.
